```{python}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

BG = "#f4f5f7"          # very light grey background for the whole chart
GRID = "#ffffff"
HIST_COLOUR = "#1f4e79"
EXPECT_COLOUR = "#E36A27"   # dashed orange expectation lines

# Illustrative approximations of annual average UK 5-year government bond yields (%), 1996-2026.
# They follow the broad historic shape of the series. Replace with official data before publishing.
HIST_YEARS = np.arange(1996, 2027)
HIST_5Y = np.array([
    7.6, 6.9, 5.5, 5.0, 5.3, 4.6, 4.3, 4.2, 4.5, 4.2, 4.6,   # 1996-2006
    5.2, 4.0, 2.7, 2.5, 1.9, 1.0, 1.6, 1.7, 1.2, 0.7, 0.7,   # 2007-2017
    1.1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.6, 2.8, 4.3, 4.0, 4.0, 3.8,              # 2018-2026
])
assert len(HIST_YEARS) == len(HIST_5Y)

def smooth_line(x, y, steps=12):
    # Catmull-Rom spline: passes through every annual point, so expectation markers stay on the line
    xs, ys = [], []
    n = len(x)
    for i in range(n - 1):
        p0 = y[max(i - 1, 0)]
        p1 = y[i]
        p2 = y[i + 1]
        p3 = y[min(i + 2, n - 1)]
        for t in np.linspace(0, 1, steps, endpoint=False):
            v = 0.5 * ((2 * p1) + (-p0 + p2) * t + (2 * p0 - 5 * p1 + 4 * p2 - p3) * t**2
                       + (-p0 + 3 * p1 - 3 * p2 + p3) * t**3)
            xs.append(x[i] + t * (x[i + 1] - x[i]))
            ys.append(v)
    xs.append(x[-1]); ys.append(y[-1])
    return np.array(xs), np.array(ys)

SMOOTH_X, SMOOTH_Y = smooth_line(HIST_YEARS.astype(float), HIST_5Y)

# Theoretical expectations: at each 5-year point, the expected 5-year yield path over the next
# five years, reverting from the yield prevailing at that point towards a long-run level.
LONG_RUN = 3.5
REVERSION = 0.25   # speed of reversion per year
HORIZON = 5
EXPECT_YEARS = np.arange(1996, 2027, 1)   # an expectation every year

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
fig.patch.set_facecolor(BG)
ax.set_facecolor(BG)

# Forecast zone, the five years after the last historic point
ax.axvspan(2026, 2031, color="#e6e9ee", zorder=0)

ax.plot(SMOOTH_X, SMOOTH_Y, color=HIST_COLOUR, linewidth=2.4, zorder=3)

for i, t0 in enumerate(EXPECT_YEARS):
    y0 = HIST_5Y[HIST_YEARS == t0][0]
    s = np.linspace(t0, t0 + HORIZON, 26)
    path = LONG_RUN + (y0 - LONG_RUN) * np.exp(-REVERSION * (s - t0))
    ax.plot(s, path, color=EXPECT_COLOUR, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=(0, (5, 3)), zorder=2)
    ax.plot([t0], [y0], marker="o", markersize=4, color=EXPECT_COLOUR, zorder=4)

ax.set_xlim(1995.5, 2031.5)
ax.set_ylim(0, 9)
ax.set_xticks(range(1996, 2032, 5))
ax.set_ylabel("5-year yield (%)", color="#495057")
ax.tick_params(colors="#495057")
ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, linewidth=1.0, zorder=1)
for side in ("top", "right", "left", "bottom"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)

handles = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=HIST_COLOUR, linewidth=2.4, label="Historic 5-year yield"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=EXPECT_COLOUR, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=(0, (5, 3)),
           label="Theoretical expectation, next 5 years"),
]
ax.legend(handles=handles, frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper right")
fig.text(0.5, 0.975, "Illustrative government bond yields: history and expectations",
         fontsize=12.5, fontweight="bold", color="#212529", ha="center", va="top")
plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93))
plt.show()
```
:::

<p class="chart-note">Illustrative visualisation of UK 5-year government bond (gilt) yields. Historic values are approximate; expectations are theoretical, not a forecast or investment advice.</p>
